The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 43 from Ben Stokes, complemented by a commanding 67-run stand between Jos Buttler and Ben Stokes that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 2.99 RPO. West Indies's bowling response was spearheaded by JO Holder (6/41), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Folded for 204/10 (67.3 ov), England suffered an early setback, conceding vital first-innings momentum to West Indies.

The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 95 from J Blackwood, complemented by a commanding 73-run stand between J Blackwood and RL Chase that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 3.09 RPO. England's bowling response was spearheaded by JC Archer (3/40), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Reaching 200/6 (64.2 ov), West Indies successfully completed a historic fourth-innings pursuit to seal an emphatic victory.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at The Rose Bowl commenced with high tactical intensity as England posted 204/10 (67.3 ov) in their opening innings. In response, West Indies countered with 318/10 (101.6 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 6-Wicket Spell: JO Holder (6/41), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Ben Stokes delivered a masterclass for England (89 Runs & 6 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (West Indies 64%) and allowing West Indies to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, England faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. West Indies's bowling unit, bolstered by ST Gabriel (4 Runs & 9 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing West Indies won by 4 wickets in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: West Indies's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While England produced fighting phases, West Indies won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
